macro.regime: Deleveraging risk-off into a hawkish Fed hold; Mideast war premium on oil
macro.narrative: As of Fri 23 Oct US/Asia close, global markets are mid a broad cross-asset deleveraging rather than a classic flight-to-safety: US equities extended a choppy two-week drawdown (S&P -2.3%, Nasdaq -4.7% from 12 Oct highs) while Japan (-10.5% from 8 Oct) and Korea (-18% from 7 Oct) suffered outright crashes driven mainly by AI-capex-monetization doubts and Chinese memory-chip oversupply (CXMT) undercutting Samsung/SK Hynix, amplified by a hot September US CPI (3.7% y/y) that revived rate-hike fear rather than by the Mideast war itself. That same inflation print, plus this week's firmer core-PCE (f'cast 0.3%) and GDP (f'cast 3.2%) data, sets up a hawkish FOMC hold on Thu 29 Oct (market pricing ~94% hold at 3.75-4.00%, ~6% hike tail) with the 10-year near 5.00% and a normally-sloped curve (10s2s +31bp) -- no recession signal from rates, but little room for the dovish pivot risk assets want, and a strong dollar (DXY ~102, near 18-month highs). Credit is a genuine early-warning flag, not yet a crisis: HY OAS widened from 327bp to 340bp over the past week and CCC OAS blew out to a 100th-percentile-since-2023 1,340bp, with stress concentrated in the weakest issuers. Mideast risk is real and escalating -- confirmed Houthi drone strikes on Aramco's ~1mbd Shaybah field and on the Hormuz-bypass East-West pipeline pushed Brent above $110 -- but gold, silver and Bitcoin all fell alongside equities this week (Bitcoin through $800M+ weekend liquidations and BlackRock/Fidelity-led spot-ETF outflows), confirming this is a margin-call/liquidation event across leveraged commodity, crypto and APAC-tech positions rather than a safe-haven bid, which is the key risk-management read for anyone running leverage into this tape.
